requirements.requirement: Establish a three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: etcd 3.5.17 was installed fresh on all three nodes (none had it), a systemd unit and config were created, firewall ports 2379/2380 opened, and the cluster was bootstrapped. Member list shows all three members 'started' and healthy (cmd-e5431965b0504d8c). Four application keys were written from node1 and confirmed readable from node3's own endpoint (cmd-07a8ebc2703749e1, cmd-e01fae350f51481e), directly showing the healthy 3-member baseline with data present on all members.

requirements.requirement: Handle permanent loss of the node3 member (data unrecoverable) while preserving cluster quorum/availability
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped/disabled and /var/lib/etcd deleted, simulating unrecoverable data loss (cmd-79c2521caeda443a). The dead member was then removed from the cluster via etcdctl issued from node1, and the remaining node1+node2 pair was directly confirmed healthy afterward, showing quorum was preserved during the disruption (cmd-2e2579a2f2394dff). This demonstrates the required healthy-baseline -> disruption -> still-available transition for the surviving members.

requirements.requirement: Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node3 host, returning the cluster to 3 healthy members with existing keys intact
requirements.summary: A new member was registered via `member add` and node3 was reconfigured with `initial-cluster-state: existing` and restarted (cmd-f339cac8d7a04364, cmd-529c7418b6204595). Post-replacement, the member list shows 3 'started' members with matching raft term/applied index across all endpoints (cmd-1ee77dc7820843f2), and all four original application keys were confirmed intact via node3's own client endpoint (cmd-1a826e09bb024143), directly showing full restoration to a healthy 3-member cluster with the same data.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence on every managed node
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3, a pre-restart boot_id/healthy-cluster/keys baseline was captured, `systemctl reboot` was acknowledged (connection closed), SSH was unreachable during the transition, a new distinct boot_id was observed post-restart, and etcd active state, 3-member membership, and application keys were reconfirmed after each reboot before moving to the next node. This matches the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check (boot_id changed for all three nodes between snapshots).

overall_summary: The executor built a fresh 3-member etcd cluster on node1/node2/node3, wrote application keys, directly demonstrated the required healthy-baseline -> node3-loss-with-quorum-preserved -> replacement-member-restored-healthy transition with matching raft indices and intact keys, and additionally completed the mandatory per-node restart protocol with clear boot-identity changes and full post-reboot recovery on all three nodes. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The only hygiene concern is unremoved etcd installation artifacts left in /tmp on all three nodes, a minor, low-risk residue.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (timed out) at all lifecycle phases on all nodes, so package database integrity cannot be independently verified from this evidence.

The node3 'permanent loss' scenario was executor-simulated (manual stop/wipe) rather than an externally injected failure, which is consistent with the task's premise but means the disruption timing and mechanism were fully executor-controlled.
Leftover /tmp installation artifacts (etcd.tar.gz, extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64) were not cleaned up on any of the three nodes after task completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor-caused mutations were reviewed chronologically. Package/service installation (binary copy, mkdir/chown, systemd unit, etcd.conf.yml) on all three nodes were necessary prerequisites. The first `systemctl enable --now etcd` attempt (cmd-40959533baea4ebd) timed out because firewall ports were not yet open; the subsequent firewall-cmd port-opening (cmd-dd36d0c5d1064b80 et al.) and the `stop etcd; rm -rf /var/lib/etcd/*; start etcd` retry (cmd-7a01701d2c3641ce et al.) on all three nodes were corrective actions needed to recover from that failed first bootstrap attempt, not gratuitous experiments — reasonable and bounded. Read-only diagnostics (nc missing, /dev/tcp probes, ping, iptables -L) caused no state change. The main unaddressed hygiene issue is leftover installation residue: the downloaded etcd.tar.gz and extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory remain in /tmp on all three nodes after task completion (visible in after_executor temporary-files diffs), which was never cleaned up. This is a low-risk, bounded residue (disk space only, no security exposure) but was retained rather than reverted. No failed services, damaged package state, or unsafe exposure were observed in the final snapshots.
